messages:
SamW: Heads-up — microbench on SM92 showed a regression in token throughput after yesterday's autotuner push. Repro steps below.
MayaR: Ugh, details?
SamW: Batch 8, seqlen 512, model: gpt-like, heads=30 (non-power-of-two). Autotuner picked fused-sdpa-v3-causal-prefetch kernel but latency shot up ~26% compared to baseline.
TomasL: Heads=30 is weird — our heuristics usually map odd heads to fallback, maybe autotuner mis-scored. Any KV cache differences?
SamW: Yes that's the thing — KV cache warmup pattern changed, microprofiling shows extra L2 thrash on the kernel's prefetch path. Attached perf snippet:
```
PMU: L2_TLB_MISS +42%
SMEM_BANK_CONFLICT +18%
warp_stalls +12%
```
MayaR: Can you paste the autotuner scoring for that probe run?
SamW: Score block:
```
probe_id=4512
candidate=fused-sdpa-v3-prefetch
score=0.72
fallback=fused-sdpa-v2
```
MayaR: Score looks off — we weight memory latency lower for SM92 recently. Maybe a config drift.
TomasL: I can reproduce with local repro. Looks like our warmup uses microbatch=1 which doesn't fill KV cache well; autotuner tests used microbatch=4 — mismatch.
QA_Nick: I ran the end-to-end test and saw token p99 spikes on regional-prod-2 around 16:43 UTC. Alert fired.
InfraBot: Deploy 2026-03-17T16:35:22 by maya_r completed to canary.
MayaR: Proposal: revert autotuner commit that inverted mem vs compute weight, and add probe variant that measures KV cache steady-state (longer warmup). Rollout to canary first.
SamW: Agreed. Also add fallback rule when head_size % 8 != 0 AND seq_len >= 256 to force conservative kernel until fix.
TomasL: I'll open a short PR with revert + extra probe and a unit test that runs head sizes 7..33 across seqlen [128,512].
MayaR: Thanks. @SamW can you attach perf traces and the reproducer script?
SamW: uploading now to /internal/perf/2276543210-repro.tar.gz
MayaR: leaving a note to run on SM92 only — different on SM80. I'll schedule canary tomorrow morning.
QA_Nick: After fix please run the load test with KV cache primed for 5k tokens.
SamW: Will do. :thumbsup:
